# LevelStatistics

Module: **core** · directory: `src/Programs` · binary: `src/Programs/LevelStatistics`

```text
LevelStatistics, version 0.01

Usage: LevelStatistics [options] 

Options:

system options:
    -s, --spectrum : name of the file that contains the spectrum
    --multiple-spectra : column formated ASCII file that lists all the spectra to analyze
    -c, --energy-column : index of the column that contains the energies (0 being the first column) (default value = 1)
    --min-column : index of the first column that gives the quantum numbers (0 being the first column) (default value = 0)
    --max-column : index of the last column that gives the quantum numbers (negative if it is the one just before the energy column) (default value = -1)
    -d, --degeneracy-column : index of the optional column that contains the energies degeneracy not appearing explicitly in the spectrum (must be larger than energy-column) (default value = 0)
    --z2-symmetry : assume that the spectrum is invariant under the transformation Q<->-Q and that only the Q>=0 are available in the spectrum
    --unfold-spectrum : unfold the spectrum using the tabulated density of states in an ASCII file
    --filter-column : if equal or greater than 0, apply a filter on the corresponding quantum number column (default value = -1)
    --filter-value : value of the quantum number that should be kept if --filter-value is applied (default value = 0)
    --window-min : when having a single quantum number sector, set the index of the first eigenvalue to consider (default value = 0)
    --window-max : when having a single quantum number sector, set the index of the last eigenvalue to consider (negative if up to the last available eigenvalue) (default value = -1)
    --discard-quantumnumbers : do not perform the level statistics per quantum number sector

output options:
    -o, --output-file : name of the output file where the level statistics will be stored (if none, try to deduce it from either --spectrum or --multiple-spectra replacing the dat extension with levelstat)
    -b, --bin-spacing : spacing range for each bin (default value = 0.10000000000000001)

misc options:
    -h, --help : display this help

global options:
    --append-cmdline : append command line to file
```
